deep.reconstruction:
Context: these are working notes from meridian-circle observations at Göttingen, probably about 1819–20. The date is not certain: Monday 27 / Tuesday 28 fits December 1819 or September 1819. The instrument is a meridian circle read by three microscopes: U (unten, lower, near 0°), L (near 270°) and R (near 90°). It also has an 'Index' (alidade) carrying a level ('Libelle'). Nothing on the page is mathematics beyond arithmetic means and differences. It records instrument calibration.

(1) Star observations, continued from the previous page (night of Monday 27).
- Sirius: transits over three wires at 6h36m56.9s, 37m13.8s and 37m30.8s. The middle-wire time equals the mean of the outer wires: (56.9 + 90.8)/2 = 73.85 s, i.e. 37m13.85s.
- Sirius circle reading: 68°7'41.7". The further entries 2'10.4" and 1'44.6" are the minutes/seconds read at the other microscopes, in the same format as Spica and Arcturus on the previous page.
- Pollux: transits at 7h33m58.1s, 34m16.4s (a digit is overwritten) and 34m35.5s. The outer-wire mean is 34m16.8s. Circle reading 23°13'29.9", with further readings 2'57.4" and 2'35.3".
- Meteorology lines '27z 6l 6, +11°1' and '27z 6l 5, +11°3': barometer 27 Paris inches 6.6 (resp. 6.5) lines; thermometer +11.1° (resp. 11.3°), presumably Réaumur.
- My consistency check: at Göttingen (φ ≈ 51.5°), with circa-1820 declinations Sirius ≈ −16°28' and Pollux ≈ +28°27', the zenith distances are about 68°0' and 23°5'. Both readings therefore carry a common offset of about 8', matching the U zero point 0°8'25" found below.

(2) 'Dinstag 28', level readings.
- Each of three columns is read with the level in two positions:
  - Column 1: 9'10.15" and 9'4.3", mean 9'7.2" (exact 9'7.225").
  - Column 2: 3'35.05" and 3'29.3", mean 3'32.2" (exact 3'32.175").
  - Column 3: 3'17.0" and 3'11.6", mean written 3'14.2" (exact 3'14.3").
- The mean of the two level positions eliminates the level's own error. This gives the reading of each microscope when the index is level, i.e. its zenith/horizon reference.

(3) Relation of the microscope zero points, from two trials with the index at 0° and at 11°.
- Index 0°: U = 0°8'38.5", L = 269°58'13.8", R = 90°2'56.5".
- Index 11°: U = 11°8'11.3", L = 280°57'36.8", R = 101°2'19.1".
- 'Mittel', after removing the 11° shift: U = 0°8'25" (exact 24.9"), L = 269°57'55" (55.3"), R = 90°2'38" (37.8").
- Implicit content of the later remark (my computation of the differences):
  - L − U: 269°49'35.3" at index 0°, 269°49'25.5" at index 11°.
  - R − U: 89°54'18.0" and 89°54'7.8".
  - L − R: 179°55'17.3" and 179°55'17.7".
- So L and R keep their mutual distance to 0.4". The lower microscope U shifts by about 10" relative to both.

(4) Adjustment.
- 'Now the index was bent and the carrier of the lower microscope adjusted.' Result: U = 0°5'0", L = 270°0'10.0", R = 90°4'51.9".
- Check: L − R = 179°55'18.1", consistent with before. U has been set to exactly 5'0". The next page continues with index 0' and U on 5'0", L ≈ 10", R ≈ 4'52".

(5) Level at 12h.
- Rows: (3'29.5", 3'35.7", 3'21.9") and (3'23.7", 3'29.9", 3'16.1").
- Means: 3'26.6", 3'32.8", 3'19.0". All correct; the row difference is a uniform 5.8".

(6) Diagnosis.
- Gauss writes that the inequalities in the microscope differences are probably due to stretching of the cords (Schnüre) that carry the microscopes.
- The cords were tied shorter in the afternoon and new readings taken. These readings, at 24 circle positions, appear on the next page. There they are fitted with a periodic term −0.79" cos x + 0.03" sin x, and a mean reading error is derived. That fit is not on this page.
errors: Level column 3 (Tuesday 28): the mean of 3'17.0" and 3'11.6" is 3'14.3", but 3'14.2" is written. This is a 0.1" slip, or one reading is misread. The row differences 5.85, 5.75, 5.4 are less uniform than usual, which suggests the 17.0 may be 16.9.
Pollux middle wire: 34m16.4s (overwritten) against an outer-wire mean of 34m16.8s. This reflects unequal wire intervals, not an error.
No genuine errors otherwise. All zero-point means agree with the data to within rounding to whole seconds.

results.what: Elimination of the level's own error by averaging readings in two (reversed) level positions
results.modern_name: Level reversal / determination of zenith point via alidade level
results.usually_credited_to: standard 18th–19th c. instrumental practice (Reichenbach, Borda era)

results.what: Determination of the relative zero points of three circle microscopes by readings at two index positions (0° and 11°), and detection that one microscope (U) drifts about 10" relative to the diametrically opposite pair L–R
results.modern_name: Microscope zero-point / run calibration of a divided circle
results.usually_credited_to: standard observatory practice; Bessel systematized circle-error investigation (1810s–1820s)

results.what: Attributing the instability to stretching of the cords supporting the microscope carriers, and correcting it by shortening them

deep.surprise_reason: Routine observing log and instrument calibration: wire transits, circle readings, level means, microscope zero points. It is known that Gauss observed with the Göttingen meridian circles from 1819–20. The only mildly interesting part (the harmonic fit of circle errors) is on the next page.

checkable.asserts: Sirius: the outer-wire mean equals the middle wire. Times are seconds after 6h36m, i.e. 56.9 and 90.8 averaging to 73.85 (= 37m13.85s); the expression equals 0.
Level column 3 mean = 14.3" (written 14"2, a slip of 0.1").
L mean: (58'13.8" + 57'36.8")/2 = 3475.3" = 57'55.3" past 269° (expression returns 3475.3 - 10800 offset form; compare minutes 57'55").
The L−R difference changes by only −0.4" between index 0° and 11°.
The L−U difference changes by 9.8" between the two index positions, which is the 'Ungleichheit' noted.
After adjustment L−R = 179°55'18.1", consistent with 179°55'17.5" before (expression = 0).
Level means at 12h = [26.6, 32.8, 19.0] seconds past 0°3', as written.

transcription_corrections: '27' 26"6' should read '27z 6l 6' (barometer 27 Paris inches 6.6 lines), followed by '+11°1' (thermometer). Likewise '27. 6,5 +11,3' is 27z 6l 5, +11°3.
'Diärtz [?] 28' should read 'Dinstag 28' (Tuesday the 28th), following 'Montag 27' on the previous page.
Pollux middle-wire time '7.34.16,4': a digit is overwritten (struck 4/7). The outer-wire mean would be 16.8.
Under 'Jetzt wurde der Index' there is a faint pencil note '0.10.30', not in the machine transcription.
Sirius reading line: '68°7'41"7 2'10"4 1'44"6'. The last two are readings of the other microscopes (minutes/seconds), as in the previous page's format.
Level labels at the right of the 12h readings ('Spi', 'Spia') are uncertain. They label the two level positions, cf. 'Spi.' / 'auss.' on the previous page.
After the adjustment the R reading is '90°4'51"9' (degrees 90, minutes 4, seconds 51.9).
